source.note: hand-written; a car-maintenance voice note with numbers that must survive exactly

units.text: Car stuff. The Yaris is at a hundred and seventy-eight thousand kilometres, oil change is due at one eighty, so in about two thousand, call it a month the way I drive. Pan Zbyszek, the garage on Głogowska, not the dealer, the dealer wanted six hundred for the same oil change and Zbyszek does it for three fifty.
Insurance renews on the first of June. Last year it was fourteen hundred with Link4, get a quote from PZU this time, Bartek said he pays way less for a similar car.
The right rear tyre is slowly losing pressure, like, point two bar a week. Probably a nail. Ask Zbyszek to look at it when I bring it in for the oil, don't make a separate trip.
And the winter tyres are in the basement, in the cage, not in the garage, because the garage flooded last year. Swap them back in, uh, October.

expected.content: The user's Toyota Yaris is at about 178,000 km; the next oil change is due at 180,000 km, about a month away as of April 2026.
The user takes the Yaris to Pan Zbyszek's garage on Głogowska, not the dealer: the dealer quoted 600 PLN for an oil change that Zbyszek does for 350.
The car insurance renews on June 1; last year it cost 1,400 PLN with Link4, and the user plans to get a PZU quote because Bartek pays much less for a similar car.
The Yaris's right rear tyre loses about 0.2 bar a week, probably a nail; the user will have Zbyszek check it at the oil change rather than make a separate trip.
The user's winter tyres are stored in the basement cage, not the garage (which flooded in 2025); they go back on in October.
